title: Hilary Duff ate New England clam chowder and a Dunkin’ Munchkin on stage during her Mass. concert
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Hilary Duff tasted New England clam chowder and Dunkin' Munchkins on stage at Xfinity Center in Mansfield, Massachusetts.
During her 'The Lucky Me Tour', Duff tries local foods at each stop; she expressed initial apprehension about the chowder.
Duff enjoyed the chowder's broth and emphasized it was 'wicked good', while also successfully catching a Munchkin in her mouth.

title: Adley Rutschman ready to make his debut with Red Sox on Tuesday
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman is set to debut for the Boston Red Sox against the Toronto Blue Jays on Tuesday.
Rutschman was acquired from the Orioles on August 3 and has been recovering from wrist inflammation.
Boston may not initially give Rutschman an everyday catching role, easing him into the lineup.

title: Springfield zoo suffers devastating damage during severe storm
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The Zoo in Forest Park in Springfield closed indefinitely after severe storm damage, uprooting trees and destroying enclosures.
Despite no animal injuries among 200 present, intense winds and thunderstorms caused substantial zoo damage.
Zoo faces financial impact from closure, with lost revenue and unexpected cleanup costs; donations welcomed online.

title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people were killed in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough, Massachusetts.
The crash occurred before 3 p.m. on I-290 East, prompting a response from State Police, Marlborough Fire, and EMS.
The Solomon Pond Road exit was closed Monday evening, causing traffic delays and urging drivers to find alternate routes.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A body was recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury after a possible drowning report on Sunday.
Search efforts involved divers, sonar technology, and drones, but the man was not located until Monday morning.
The victim's identity has not been released, and the investigation into the drowning incident is ongoing.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Khalil Jacobs, an undrafted linebacker, is impressing at the New England Patriots' training camp.
Jacobs had a productive 2025 season at the University of Missouri but went undrafted in 2026.
Initially overlooked, Jacobs is emerging as a depth option in the Patriots' thin linebacker corps.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed a law removing gestational limits on abortions in Massachusetts, allowing them based on physicians' judgment.
The law removes previous restrictions that required medical reviews for abortions at 24 weeks or later, easing access to late-term abortions.
Opponents argue the law reduces protections for unborn children, while supporters say it ensures better access to necessary healthcare.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The gravestone of a free Black man named Sebastian, who died in 1729, was restored in Boston's Granary Burying Ground.
The stone is believed to be the oldest gravestone for a free Black person in the U.S., found during a conservation project.
Sebastian, once enslaved, advocated for his and his wife's marriage, influencing early antislavery and marriage rights advocacy.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots' Carlton Davis returns to practice with limited participation, while Will Campbell fully participates after injury absences.
Romeo Doubs impresses with a highlight-reel touchdown catch, and Kyle Williams showcases speed with a deep ball reception.
Marcus Lomu continues to learn multiple line positions, practicing at left tackle with the second-team during Monday's session.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A lifeguard at Scarborough Beach, Maine, was pulled underwater by a white shark while using a rescue torpedo.
The shark encounter prompted the closure of the beach for an hour as officials monitored the waters.
Scarborough officials warned of increased white shark sightings, advising caution and reporting any sightings to lifeguards.
